segments.source: I n the olden days, the people buried some men on a hill.
Then they removed their camp to another place.
Many winters afterwards, a man visited the hill; but there were no graves there.
Then many men came and dug far down into the hill.
By and by a man said, “There is a road here.”
There they found a road, a tunnel, large enough for men to walk, stooping.
They followed the first road and they came to a place where a strange animal had dragged the bodies of those who were buried in the hill.
Therefore the people refused to bury their dead in the ground.
They bury them on scaffolds where the animals cannot reach them.

At the present day, the Teton gives three reasons for not burying in the ground: animals or persons might walk over the graves; the dead might lie in mud and water after rain or snow; wolves might trouble the bodies.
